key_insight: The paper shows that distributed quantum computing can be made scalable by using a weak-coupling approximation, reducing classical reconstruction cost from exponential to polynomial when a circuit can be partitioned around weakly coupled qubits.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical quantum circuit knitting for larger problems by lowering the classical overhead of distributed execution, especially for layered variational circuits such as those used in QAOA.
method: Partition the quantum procedure across a qubit weakly coupled to the rest of the circuit.
Use a controlled approximation to reconstruct the global process with polynomial classical cost.
Demonstrate the approach on layered QAOA-like circuits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a demonstration on a layered circuit based on QAOA circuits, showing the method on a representative benchmark family.
watch_item: The approximation depends on a weak-coupling assumption, so accuracy and applicability may degrade when inter-qubit coupling is strong or the partition is not natural.
paper_title: Scalable quantum circuit knitting using a weak-coupling approximation
